name: Burg Laudegg
kurzbeschreibung: The picturesque hilltop fortress Burg Laudegg towers above the castle pond in Ladis on a steep slate crag with its Romanesque stone keep.
beschreibung:
Overview

The distinctive and far-visible Laudegg Castle (Burg Laudegg, historically also known as Laudeck) rises dramatically on a sheer slate cliff high above the historic village of Ladis on the sunny Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis high plateau. Paired with the tranquil, reed-fringed Lader castle pond resting at its base, the fortress forms one of the most beloved and photographed picture-postcard landmarks in the entire Upper Inn Valley. First documented in 1220, this proud hilltop fortification served for centuries as the judicial and administrative stronghold for the Counts of Tyrol. Today, the lovingly restored private castle complex stands as a majestic sentinel overlooking the alpine amphitheater of surrounding three-thousand-meter peaks.

Route & Requirements

The architectural core of the medieval complex is its mighty, four-sided Romanesque keep dating from the early 13th century, crafted from meticulously dressed quarry stone to serve as a formidable defensive haven. Adjacent structures include the restored palas, historic curtain walls, and remnants of defensive parapets. A level, stroller-friendly footpath encircles the castle pond, in whose glassy surface the sheer castle walls mirror spectacularly. Well-designed educational panels along the shoreline narrate the fortification's colorful past, chivalric feuds, courthouse sessions, and devastating fires that afflicted the structure in centuries past. During summer, weekly guided walks grant exclusive access to the picturesque inner courtyard, castle chapel, and gate tower.

Visit & Arrival

The outdoor grounds, castle pond, and panoramic viewpoints are freely accessible around the clock year-round free of charge. Guided castle tours operate from June through September on designated weekdays (registration through the Ladis tourist board recommended). Arrival by car: take the Inntal autobahn A12 to the Oberinntal interchange, continue on federal road B180 to Ried im Oberinntal, and ascend via state road L19 to the sunny Ladis plateau; free parking is located at the village entrance. By public transit: ÖBB train to Landeck-Zams station, connecting with hourly VVT bus route 220 directly to Ladis center.

Tips

Combine your walk around the pond with a refreshing stop at the historic Ladis Sauerbrunn Spring, Tyrol's oldest documented medicinal mineral spring, where visitors can taste the naturally effervescent mineral water for free. Families will adore the themed water trail leading from the lake through gentle larch forests, offering breathtaking vistas of the Upper Inn Valley and Samnaun mountain range. Conclude your excursion with traditional Tyrolean dishes in a welcoming local tavern.
preis: Exterior and castle pond free of charge; guided tours approx. €6.00
oeffnungszeiten: Exteriors accessible year-round; interior visits in summer via weekly guided tours
